pairs.why: A is a well-built locomotive with cowcatcher and tender and smooth painted shading like the bus/coaster cards, while B is blockier and reads as a plastic toy with an odd flat front plate.
A has chunky, smoothly painted posts and planks with a plausibly hung life ring, while B's photo-like caustic water and floating ring are more texture-heavy and less like the real stylized water.
B's round anchor badge and overhanging soft white crown match the real hat's build more closely than A's hexagonal badge and stiff frontal view.
A matches the real navy tone, sharp flukes and vertical-stripe background, while B is a glossy bulbous toy on diagonal stripes, the 'too glossy' failure from the lessons.
A is a saturated, smoothly rendered console with a clear build like the real cards, while B is flat, dull and oddly built as a cabinet with a drawer.
B keeps the real chair's construction (no armrests, X legs, looped base) while A turns it into an armchair, a different object despite richer rendering.
A has labelled keys and real calculator proportions like the real card, while B's blank keys make it a non-functional object despite closer key colours.
B is a believable white astronaut helmet with clean saturated rendering, while A is a blue-orange ball on a pedestal that reads as a toy rather than a real object.
